_comment: Single source of truth for what may be published. Edit thresholds here, never in code. Every value is enforced by scripts/compliance-gate.mjs before any upload.

youtube_limits._source: YouTube Help: Add video metadata, and Shorts eligibility requirements.

repetition._comment: Defends against the YouTube 'Mass-produced or repetitive content' policy, which is the single largest existential risk to a daily automated channel.

kid_safety._comment: Two tiers. hard_banned is blocked outright with no appeal. context_sensitive words are legitimate in educational science and history but need a judgement call, so they raise a warning and are referred to the AI safety reviewer. A flat list blocked 'jellyfish have no blood', which is why the split exists.
kid_safety._context_note: These appear constantly in legitimate nature, science and history facts. Venomous animals, blood chemistry, historical wars, viruses in biology. Blocking them outright would gut the topic library.

house_style._comment: Owner's stated brand rules. Violations are hard blocks because they ship into the public title and description.

metadata_integrity._comment: Guards against the YouTube 'Spam, deceptive practices and scams' policy: misleading metadata and keyword stuffing.

legal._comment: Copyright and consumer-law exposure. Audio is the highest-frequency real risk: Content ID claims on background beds routinely strip monetisation.
legal._trademark_note: Nominative reference in an educational fact is fine. Implying endorsement, partnership or official status is not.

coppa._comment: US COPPA and the YouTube made-for-kids setting. Getting this wrong carries FTC penalties, so it is asserted explicitly rather than left to a default.

ai_panel._comment: Independent model reviewers for judgement calls the rule engine cannot make. Requires a majority to pass.

reviewers.focus: Is every factual claim verifiably true and current?
Is this safe and appropriate for a broad audience including minors?
Any copyright, trademark, defamation or advertising-disclosure risk?
Does the title honestly represent the content, free of clickbait?

enforcement._comment: block = refuse to upload. warn = upload but record. strict_mode escalates every warn to a block.
